conviction_note: Nothing decisive and company-level was found: the closest counterparty (First Hawaiian, reported 2026-10-23) printed Hawaii deposit costs down and NIM above its own guide, which supports BOH's 2.9% year-end NIM path, set against a single-name CRE charge-off at FHB and three Q3 storms that cut August visitor spending 9.7%; the findings sum to +0.5 and the scaled number is a near-coin-flip lean (p_up 53) on a 4.8% absolute move, so the two measurements agree in sign and the scaled one is smaller because the evidence is proxy and counterparty, not BOH's own number.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $1.51 on revenue $202.6M (Investing.com preview, 2026-10-23, https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/bank-of-hawaii-earnings-up-next-can-margin-gains-continue-93CH-4928901) and $1.52 on revenue $202.3M (Benzinga, Oct 2 snapshot, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BOH/earnings-forecasts) -- two sources agree within a cent. Revenue bar $202.6M implies +$5.7M (+2.9%) over Q2's $196.9M (NII $153.6M + noninterest income $43.3M, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046195/000004619526000054/ex991earningsrelease063026.htm). Company guide (Q2 call, 2026-07-28, via https://www.webull.com/news/15303749301904384): NIM 'gets to 2.90% by the end of the year' from 2.78% in Q2, conditional on one rate hike plus fixed-asset repricing; FY expenses +2.5-3%; FY loan growth low-to-mid single digits; planned runoff of high-cost public deposits in Q3. Q2 itself was a $0.01 EPS beat with a ~$2.9M revenue miss and the stock fell 4.7%, so the revenue/NII line is what this name trades on.
positioning_check: Short interest ~3.5M shares, ~8.8% of float, 6.2 days to cover as of the 2026-08-14/08-19 settlement (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/boh/shortinterest; Curved Trading lists the same 3.5M with 12.0 days to cover on a different volume base, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/boh/short-interest/); no October settlement found (Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503). That is elevated for a regional bank. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline; front-expiry put/call OI 1.83 on only 252 contracts total with a 63% ATM spread, so the option market makes no usable directional statement. Tape: spot 70.64, -17.7% from 52w high, fell from ~77 in early September to 65.80 on 2026-10-14 (vs KRE ~-9% and FHB roughly flat over the same span), then +5.1% over the last 5 sessions with the sector bounce.

findings.finding: First Hawaiian, the closest Hawaii deposit competitor, reported Q3 on 2026-10-23 with NIM up 5bp to 3.30% (above the 3.27% it had projected for Q3), interest-bearing deposit cost down 3bp to 1.72% from 1.75% despite the 2026-09-16 Fed hike, and total deposits up $50M after a $623M Q2 outflow -- evidence that Hawaii deposit competition, which BOH's CEO called 'elevated' in July and named as the risk to its 2.9% NIM path, eased in Q3; BOH needs roughly +6bp NIM plus day count to hit the $202.6M revenue bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-27): NIM +4bp but revenue missed by ~$2.9M and the stock fell 4.7% despite an EPS beat; Q4 2025 print (2026-01-26) +6.09%. The revenue/NII line has moved this stock several points both ways.
findings.why_not_priced: FHB reported the same morning as this seal; BOH closed roughly flat on 2026-10-23 (70.26 to ~70.55) while FHB fell ~3.6% on its EPS miss, so the market read FHB's headline (credit) and not its deposit-cost line. If BOH had been re-rated on the read-across it would have moved with or against FHB that session; it did not. Partly priced: BOH is +5% in five sessions with KRE.
findings.independence: Sector peers that reported Q3 2026 show contained deposit costs: Regions deposit costs +1bp to 1.70% and says the September hike lifts Q4 NII as retail deposit repricing lags (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026); Columbia Banking interest-bearing deposit cost down to 1.95% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000887343/000088734326000184/colb-20260930ex991earnings.htm). Shares the FHB 8-K with the credit finding below.

findings.finding: First Hawaiian took a $20.3M Q3 provision (vs $5.6M in Q2) driven by a $12.5M partial charge-off on a single CRE loan plus other CRE downgrades, NCOs 0.60% annualized vs 0.11%; BOH disclosed in July that criticized assets rose on a single borrower it called well secured, so a Hawaii CRE credit read-across exists, though FHB did not say where the loan is.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BOH credit has been a non-event recently (Q2 NCOs 0.10%, nonaccrual $11.3M); no print in the baseline turned on credit. FHB itself fell ~3.6% on 2026-10-23 on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: BOH did not trade down with FHB on 2026-10-23, so the market treated FHB's charge-off as idiosyncratic. If it had priced a Hawaii CRE read-across BOH would have fallen with FHB. The location and property type of FHB's loan are undisclosed, so the read-across is inference.
findings.independence: BOH's own Q2 disclosure of a single-borrower criticized increase (https://www.webull.com/news/15303749301904384). Shares the FHB 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036377/000110465926118299/fhb-ex99d1.htm) with the deposit finding; FHB's allowance ratio actually fell to 1.14% from 1.15%, which argues against a broad Hawaii credit problem.

findings.finding: Hawaii took three storms in Q3 2026 -- Hurricane Lala (Aug 14-16, DBEDT estimate $3-5B in total damage and economic loss, roughly 3-5% of state GDP), Tropical Storm Moke (Aug 22-24) and Hurricane Lowell (Sept 7-8, near-total power loss on Kauai) -- and August visitor spending fell 9.7% y/y with arrivals -5.6% and the daily census -15.9%; a BOH qualitative reserve overlay, hardship deferrals or a softer loan/fee outlook is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior BOH print in the baseline turned on a natural disaster; the closest is the 2023 Maui fire, outside the baseline window and not sourced here.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: BOH fell from ~77 to ~66 between early September and mid-October while FHB was flat, which is consistent with a Hawaii-specific discount already in the stock. What is not yet visible is BOH's own reserve and deferral number. The counterparty evidence cuts against a large hit: FHB's Q3 release does not mention the storms and its allowance ratio fell.
findings.independence: AP storm coverage of Lowell's Kauai damage (https://www.local10.com/news/national/2026/09/08/hawaiis-western-islands-hit-by-fierce-winds-from-hurricane-lowell-leaving-extensive-damage/); Hawaii State FCU activated a Lala deferral program (https://www.cuinsight.com/press-release/hawaii-state-fcu-activates-emergency-relief-program-for-members-impacted-by-hurricane-lala/). Proxy: macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by BOH.

findings.finding: The condition BOH put on its 2.90% year-end NIM target -- one 25bp hike -- was met: the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, so the call should reaffirm the guide rather than walk it back, and Regions reported the hike lifts Q4 NII as deposit repricing lags.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NIM guide has been the call's main line; Q2's -4.7% came with a revenue miss despite a reiterated NIM path, so reaffirmation alone has not bought this stock much.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the hike is public and the guide already assumed it, so this lands inside what the company guided. What is unpriced is only whether BOH's deposit beta after the hike is low enough to keep the trajectory; FHB's Q3 deposit cost suggests it is.
findings.independence: Regions Q3 2026 commentary (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026); CFO quote on the conditional guide (https://www.webull.com/news/15303749301904384).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: ~8.8% of float short with 6-12 days to cover at the August settlement, the stock -17.7% from its 52-week high and lagging FHB by ~13 points since early September, into an in-line bar ($1.51-1.52 EPS, two sources agree) -- an in-line or better NII line meets a short base with several days of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze-like reaction in the baseline; the largest up move was +6.09% (2026-01-26).
findings.why_not_priced: Short data is two months stale and may have changed; the last-week +5% bounce may already be covering. If the short base had covered, short interest at the October settlements would be lower; it could not be retrieved.
findings.independence: Curved Trading FINRA-based figure, 3.5M shares, 12.0 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/boh/short-interest/) -- same underlying FINRA data.

outside_window.finding: DBEDT's September 2026 visitor statistics, which will show Hurricane Lowell's effect on arrivals and spending, are due in late October; if released after 2026-10-26 they cannot affect this window.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (reaction function): Q2 reaffirmed the NIM path and still fell 4.7% on a revenue miss, so the FHB deposit read-across trimmed from +0.8 to +0.7.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the Fed-hike finding lands inside the company's own conditional NIM guide, trimmed from +0.4 to +0.2.
Lesson 5 (proxy, macro-to-company): the storm finding is unconfirmed by BOH and partly contradicted by FHB's falling allowance ratio, trimmed from -0.4 to -0.3, kept filed.
Lesson 7 / 5 (positioning not colour, stale short data): positioning finding trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4 because the short figure is two months old.
Lesson 6 (bar): bar verified at two agreeing sources ($1.51/$1.52), so no cap applied; p_up moved 54 to 53.
